hypotheses.reasoning: Earliest anomaly: notif-db reports transaction 80804 from template-svc-reconciler ACTIVE 108s holding a row lock on notifications (#191). Shortly after, UPDATE notifications hits lock wait timeouts (#208,#219,#225), template-svc /render statements are canceled at 10s (#209,#232,#242), notification-svc TemplateClient times out at 15s (#211,#233,#244), its 50-connection pool to template-svc fills up with a growing queue (#243,#265,#271,#279), and the gateway returns 504s (#248 onward). The root resource that runs out is a DB row lock held by a long-running reconciler transaction. Everything after that is cascade.
This could also be classed as a dependency timeout: template-svc's calls to notif-db time out because of lock waits, and that spreads up through notification-svc to the gateway.
Pool saturation and 504s are a cascade, but they are a symptom of the DB lock holder, not the source.

verdict.recommendedAction: Kill the long-running template-svc-reconciler transaction (80804) on notif-db to release the row lock on notifications. Pause or fix the reconciler so it commits quickly, using short transactions and a timeout on idle transactions. Then confirm lock waits stop and the notification-svc pool to template-svc drains. Longer term: lower the template-svc client timeout below the gateway timeout and add a circuit breaker so lock contention can't use up every connection in the pool. Ignore the notif-worker GC pause and the gateway disk-usage warning; they aren't related.
